title: Python motion reaches actual CAD.
summary: A measured software connection now links the nominal motion model to a copied Rhino working model. Later port-workflow checks show why observing motion and accepting a complete saved result remain separate milestones.
dateLabel: 22 Oct 2026 · runner follow-up; 19–21 Oct CAD history retained
evidence: Accepted nominal CAD correspondence · later port workflow incomplete
heroAlt: Accepted 19 October motion connection distinguished from the later incomplete port workflow.
heroCaption: Two different gates, preserved separately. The accepted motion demonstration does not make every later CAD workflow complete.

sections.title: An actual connection, with a small scope
sections.text: On 19 October, the unchanged Python foundation drove a copied partial piston model and synthetic crank, rod and cylinder in Rhino 7. Actual document geometry was read back across all 361 one-degree poses. The acceptance review passed software and geometry correspondence, including a saved/reopened working copy. This is nominal rigid-motion software evidence, not a validated assembled engine.

figure.alt: Frozen Python poses pass through a bound exchange to actual Rhino readback and independent comparison.
figure.caption: Intended transforms are not sufficient. The accepted workflow compared observations from the document with the frozen numerical core.

sections.title: What was observed rather than assumed
sections.text: The checks covered actual datum and joint positions, millimetre/unit mapping, rigid orientation, complete-cycle return, repeated poses, persistence and rejected updates. Eleven invalid-input and controlled-fault cases preserved the document or verified rollback. The CAD correspondence threshold remained 0.001 mm. The tiny observed numerical residual describes agreement between software representations; it is not the precision of manufactured hardware.

figure.alt: Four accepted facts: 361 actual poses, unchanged 0.001 millimetre threshold, 11 rejection/rollback cases and saved/reopened readback.
figure.caption: Accepted 19 October evidence. The copied piston is a partial nominal constraint model; the surrounding mechanism is synthetic.

sections.title: Keep the failed attempts in the history
sections.text: The first session stopped before geometry acceptance when a document identifier could not be serialized. A separately authorized replacement reached the geometry work. A further recording incompatibility was repaired within that same replacement session; the final motion gate passed. Original failures, source identities and resource records were retained. Successful recovery did not erase the unsuccessful attempts or change the numerical threshold.

sections.title: A later port workflow has a different unfinished gate
sections.text: The 21 October port-construction workflow again observed 361 poses, but did not earn complete runtime acceptance. Save/reopen testing first exposed layer-index renumbering. A later attempt exposed a second issue: two runtimes wrote different decimal text for identical floating-point values, so re-encoding changed an evidence hash. That is a demonstrated evidence-identity incompatibility, rather than proof that geometry changed.

figure.alt: Later port workflow separates successful replay, failed strict persistence identity, isolated causes and qualified offline corrections.
figure.caption: The accepted offline policy package passed 100 checks; a later serialization package passed 154 checks. These are separate component qualifications, not completion of the later Rhino gate.

sections.title: What the offline repair establishes
sections.text: The qualified correction binds the producer’s exact persisted bytes, then independently checks complete geometric and logical identity. It retains meaningful geometry, object/layer identity, assignments, settings, rollback and the original geometric threshold. The latest reviewed offline gate still requires a fresh runtime producer receipt and complete external gate. No later successful screenshots or completion receipt are asserted here.

sections.title: Software integration is still not physical validation
sections.text: This connection does not establish installed assembly/hull fit, hot clearance, ring-port safety, safe engine speed, combustion, power or manufacturability. The genuine progress is a reproducible connection with observed geometry and explicit failure boundaries. The 21 October runner proposal was subsequently implemented and accepted on 22 October for a small bounded supervised workload and one finite pilot. Its four model results and two expected rejections do not establish long unattended execution. The later I2 CAD runtime gate remains incomplete in the reviewed 22 October readiness record.
